subject.title: fix(media): bound hung remote downloads in media store

question: Should generic `saveMediaSource()` downloads use unconditional 30-second response-header and body-idle deadlines, or should known internal callers be allowed a longer deadline?
rationale: The lifecycle repair is technically sound, but choosing the permanent deadline changes compatibility for slow remote sources and current sibling integrations intentionally use different values.

options.title: Accept 30-second bounds
options.body: Land the focused safety default and accept that generic sources taking more than 30 seconds between network progress events will fail instead of remaining pending.

options.title: Allow an internal override
options.body: Keep safe 30-second defaults while permitting a demonstrated gateway or QA caller to request a longer deadline without creating public configuration.

options.title: Use a longer generic deadline
options.body: Increase one or both generic deadlines to reduce slow-source compatibility risk while still bounding hung downloads.

recommendation.title: Accept 30-second bounds
recommendation.body: Land the focused safety default and accept that generic sources taking more than 30 seconds between network progress events will fail instead of remaining pending.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history most strongly connects this person to both the media-store downloader and adjacent guarded-fetch behavior.
